deviations_from_card: (1) Parity is an implication, not the card's iff: openTabOf trusted => trustedAppOf offers <=> contractDriftsOf reads. The iff would make tabs_read trust a tab whose only row is an enabled host:<derived> (ADR 0105 s3 says a catalog-form row does not trust a read) - a loosening the policy-tighten gate forbids; tightening open_apps/contract check instead would shrink gated_tools (also a loosening) and break the gate-list guard. So a fifth named fold, readFold = trustFold && web-origin row enabled; pinned by its own test. (2) trustOf's off check reads records directly (any held switched-off row refuses), trust reads through known; the card's 'read records through known' for every accessor would have let a held-but-not-known off row stop refusing in disabledOriginsOf - a loosening. Only tightens open_apps/contract check for that edge (tested). origins.ts load() left unchanged. (3) One commit, not the card's two: trust.ts carries the tightening, so a behaviour-preserving first commit would have needed throwaway intermediate code. (4) Guard case 4 pinned on a 10-row matrix in trust.test.ts (expected values hand-derived from the pre-change code, green on it with a stub trust.ts) plus the unchanged existing suites, rather than re-instrumenting the fixtures of run.test.ts/run.cross-tab.test.ts/contracts.test.ts. (5) The ADR 0105 amendment is the only ADR change, as the card names; no new ADR.
